newsitem.title: ITALY: Vranitzky meets Albanian leaders on ship.
newsitem.headline: Vranitzky meets Albanian leaders on ship.

text.p: European mediator Franz Vranitzky began talks with Albanian government ministers aboard an Italian warship in the Adriatic on Friday and rebel leaders were expected to join later, officials said.
The Italian foreign ministry said the talks were taking place on the Italian frigate Aliseo.

A spokeswoman for Vranitzky's Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) mission told Reuters by telephone from the ship that rebel leaders from towns in southern Albania were expected to join later.
"We are expecting the representatives of the town committees of the insurgents to arrive on board in about two and a half hours time," she said.

Vranitzky, a former Austrian chancellor, and his delegation were taken to the ship by Italian helicopters from Brindisi and began talks with Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, Foreign Minister Arjan Starova and an army representative.

Fino, a member of Albania's opposition Socialist Party, was appointed by embattled President Sali Berisha this week to head a new government of national unity in a bid to end the armed anarchy enveloping the Balkan state, Europe's poorest country.
Representatives of the National Committee of Public Salvation, an umbrella grouping of rebel towns in southern Albania, were gathering at the Albanian port town of Vlore.

They were expected to be flown out to the Aliseo, the OSCE spokeswoman said. "We are not sure if the members of the Albanian government will stay and meet with them but that is what we hope," she added.

Western governments have pinned their hopes on the 54-member state OSCE brokering a deal with the Albanian government and rebel leaders to end an armed rebellion in the south and spreading anarchy throughout the country.
The unrest began in January over the collapse of shady pyramid savings schemes and exploded this month into insurrection in the south, where rebels have called for Berisha to quit.
Vranitzky met Berisha in Tirana last week and urged him to avoid violence in dealing with the rebellion. A top-level European Union mission also came to Tirana.
Vranitzky had planned to return to the Albanian capital on Thursday but was prevented from travelling by the deteriorating security situation and the closure of Tirana airport.

Sporadic shooting reverberated through central Tirana on Friday morning but the city appeared calmer than the previous day. Berisha and Albania's new all-party government have appealed to Europe's NATO members for military assistance to restore order.
